K9 Bond

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
They call him Bond... K9 Bond - we meet the talented SAPS Search and Rescue dog named Bond, and explore the extraordinary relationship between hound and handler.

Unique Selling Point:
Bond is attached to the SAPS K9 search and rescue unit in the Eastern Cape, and by all accounts, this Belgian Malinois is one of the best in the business.In their relatively short career together, Bond and his handler Seargent Buyisile Makhosone – affectionately known as Mak – have made quite a name for themselves. Bond has even made an appearance in the Western Cape Provincial Parliament, where he was recognised for the significant role he played in the search for survivors during the devastating George Building collapse. But it is beautiful 'bond' between MAk and Bond that make this story worth telling - they're both young, dynamic and ready to take on whatever the job throws at them.


Summary:
We had to go the full written approval route with the SAPS, and we've been approved for full access to Mak and Bond for two days. We've also got access to the whole Eastern Cape K9 unit, we can see training and demonstrations and do ride alongs etc if they are called out during our filming. We'll also get to speak to the head of the Easter Cape K9 unit. But the focus on the story will be getting to know both Mak and Bond - Sgt Makhosone is well spoken and passionate and I'm keen to find out what makes him tick.

Further information:
MAk and Bond are stationed in Lusikisiki - a small town hours from the nearest airport in the Eastern Cape. The SAPS have agreed to bring them up to Mthatha for the filming - and Mthatha has an airport.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel to Mthatha and accommodation.

Script:


K9 Bond
Final Script
29 Sept 2025


(News Audio) The death toll of the flood victims in the Eastern Cape has risen to 95

(News Audio) Through the very trees where some of the victims were clinging onto…

(News Audio) The body of another person has been recovered in Mthatha in the Eastern Cape, as the search for those missing, continues.

(Nompiliso Mchosini Subtitles)
It was on 10 June; we experienced floods while sleeping. It was around 6 AM. I was woken by my grandchild. She said, “Granny wake up - and wake up the kids, too - because it’s flooding.”

(Macfarlane) Earlier this year, torrential rain struck the Eastern Cape. As rivers burst their banks, water levels rose by more than 4m, submerging homes in the suburbs and informal settlements around Mthatha. More than 100 people died.

(Macfarlane) We met a lady that was stuck in the water for hours on end and I think you and Kat went to save her.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) I got called by Kati, in that morning of the 10th of June. He said, “Hey Mak, the situation is bad in Mthatha.” On my arrival here, joh when I’m checking here, joh it’s bad. And I can’t find Kati.

(Macfarlane) In the hours that followed, rescue teams endured an unprecedented physical and psychological challenge as they searched for survivors. Dedicated members of the Province’s K9 Unit were among them.

(Buyisile Makhosonke Subtitles) I grew up differently to other guys. I grew up where my dad is, I was always with him. And that man will always tell me, “Son, I want to teach you when you are a grown up so that you can know the way how to survive the challenges of life.”

(Buyisile Makhosonke) I’m Sergeant Buyisile Makhosonke, stationed at Lusikisiki K9, here in the Eastern Cape.

(Macfarlane) Sergeant Buyisile Makhosonke, Mak to his colleagues, is part of the Eastern Cape’s K9 Search and Rescue team – also known as Amasoeksoek.

His partner in this unique SAPS unit is 25-kilos of fur, muscle and determination. His name is Bond.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Daarsy seun. Daarsy. Ok. Sharp nê? Alright. We are going to work now. Alright? Sharp, sharp.

(Macfarlane) So that’s Bond?

(Buyisile Makhosonke) That’s Bond.

(Macfarlane) Jis, he’s a ball of energy hey? He was almost like breaking that door down, like let’s go, let’s go.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Ja. He’s like that.

(Macfarlane) And is he like this every time you guys are ready to go?

(Buyisile Makhosonke) He’s like that, ja.

(Macfarlane) We meet in Mthatha – the town Mac and Bond were deployed to during the flooding in June this year.

(Macfarlane) A lot of the times in terms of search and rescue operations you get to fields like this, where either suspects have run, or somebody has gone lost. Finding these people is an absolute nightmare. But making it easier and making it more possible is dogs like Bond.

(Macfarlane) A fellow officer is hiding a few hundred meters away, and it’s Bond’s mission to find him. Search and Rescue K9s train intensely for 5 months with one dedicated handler – and Bond only works with his partner, Mak.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Get him boy!

(Macfarlane) Once off the leash, Bond sweeps the area in a trained zig-zag pattern, making it hard for our cameras to keep up. Neither Bond nor his Mak believe in taking it slow – unfortunately this Mac was already out of breath.

(Macfarlane) So, I’ve done a lot of marathons, I’ve done a lot of long cycles… hundreds of kilometres. But this? This takes a different level of fitness, joh!

(Macfarlane) This simulation mirrors how K9’s are trained. For them, finding someone is all part of a game. Do it right, and there’s a reward.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Lekker man, seun!

(Macfarlane) The most amazing thing about this is that these working dogs work so hard and their reward is just a ball. But for someone that may have been lying there for hours or sometimes even days it means their life saved.

(Macfarlane) But search and rescue isn’t just about finding human beings. This time, we’re putting Mak’s colleagues to the test.

(Macfarlane) Sometimes it’s about finding the evidence. So I’m going to go to Kati and his partner OG, to see what they can do to find the evidence.

(Macfarlane) Mak and his mentor, Sgt Songezile -Kat-Katikati are part of an elite group – just six Search and Rescue officers covering the entire Eastern Cape.

(Macfarlane) It doesn’t take long for OG to find our ‘evidence’: a knife dropped in the veld.

(Songezile Katikati) Okay, we got it.

(Macfarlane) But even the best training can’t equip units like this for every scenario. And sometimes, the handlers must go it alone.

(News Audio) Extreme weather conditions are wreaking havoc across the Eastern Cape.

(Macfarlane) In the early hours of June 10, Nompiliso Mchosini and her four children were trapped inside their home by rising floodwaters. Her granddaughter escaped after a last-minute warning – but the door was now jammed shut.

(Nompiliso Mchosini Subtitles)
I then started banging and banging the window. I wasn’t watching what the situation was becoming behind me. When I was done breaking the window, I turned to rescue the smaller children. I saw that the children had all passed on. All of them. They were all dead.

(Macfarlane) They all passed away, mama?

(Nompiliso) They all passed away.

(Macfarlane) As pressure from the water continued to build, one of the walls of Nompiliso’s home gave way.

(Nompiliso Mchosini subtitles) As I opened my eyes, the wall just fell down. I just went like this, and jumped out. I was lucky because I found something I could hold onto. I held onto it so tight with the water pushing me. Praying and praying in the water.

(Macfarlane) Meanwhile Mak arrived on scene. Bond was held back at base – the early conditions too chaotic to deploy the K9’s.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) People are on top of the roofs, hanging in the trees. I first wanted to locate Kati first. Hey I got information that, ‘hey, that man that was rowing the boat, the water took him down.’

(Macfarlane) His mentor, Kati, had been swept down river in a rescue boat. Mak set out in a desperate attempt to find him.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) You know, that was…

(Macfarlane) Much to his relief, he came across Kati’s boat pinned against a rooftop and dived into the raging waters.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Hey, I could feel when I’m in the middle of the river, joh, this water is too much.

(Macfarlane) The power of the water?

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Yes, the power of the water, and then it took me and then I got banged against one of the roofs there.

(Macfarlane)He eventually came within shouting distance of the stricken boat.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) I can see Kati now -

(Macfarlane) Oh God.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) - and I said, “chief, what help do you want? Can you row the boat because I can see now, I’m not going to reach Kati, can you row the boat at the bottom so that I can swim to you. He said, “no, I’m with a victim here.”

(Macfarlane Subtitles) Mama Nompiliso?

(Buyisile Makhosonke Subtitles) - Yes, Mama Nompiliso.

(Macfarlane) Kati wasn’t stranded – he was with a survivor. It was Nompiliso.

(Nompiliso Mchosini Subtitles) I just want to give in at this point. I just want to give up, I’m crying and praying. As I was about to give up, the guy who rescued us came.

(Macfarlane) Unable to lift Nompiliso into his boat alone, Kati shouted for Mak to pull himself closer using a fallen electric cable.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Is the electricity off? Just imagine man, I’m in the water, I’m asking him, is the electricity off? (laughs) I swam towards the wire cable and then I grab, and then I managed to reach Kati. I had to get underneath her, and swim up strong to lift her up.

(Macfarlane) Yes.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) Kati pulled her in. That’s how we managed to save her.

(Macfarlane) Thousands were left homeless after the floods, now housed in prefab homes like these. In the immediate aftermath of the flooding, Mak, Bond and their colleagues searched tirelessly for survivors… and retrieved the bodies of those who drowned.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) I’m not a person, who if someone is in trouble, likes to sit back and watch. No. I want to be there.

(Macfarlane) Why do you keep doing it? Why do you keep doing what you do?

(Buyisile Makhosonke) What I’m doing, I love it.

(Buyisile Makhosonke) You know, that was… (Macfarlane) Much to his relief, he came across Kati’s boat pinned against a rooftop and dived into the raging waters. (Buyisile Makhosonke) Hey, I could feel when I’m in the middle of the river, joh, this water is too much. (Macfarlane) The power of the water? (Buyisile Makhosonke) Yes, the power of the water, and then it took me and then I got banged against one of the roofs there. (Macfarlane)He eventually came within shouting distance of the stricken boat. (Buyisile Makhosonke) I can see Kati now - (Macfarlane) Oh God. (Buyisile Makhosonke) - and I said, “chief, what help do you want? Can you row the boat because I can see now, I’m not going to reach Kati, can you row the boat at the bottom so that I can swim to you. He said, “no, I’m with a victim here.” (Macfarlane Subtitles) Mama Nompiliso? (Buyisile Makhosonke Subtitles) - Yes, Mama Nompiliso. (Macfarlane) Kati wasn’t stranded – he was with a survivor. It was Nompiliso. (Nompiliso Mchosini Subtitles) I just want to give in at this point. I just want to give up, I’m crying and praying. As I was about to give up, the guy who rescued us came. (Macfarlane) Unable to lift Nompiliso into his boat alone, Kati shouted for Mak to pull himself closer using a fallen electric cable. (Buyisile Makhosonke) Is the electricity off? Just imagine man, I’m in the water, I’m asking him, is the electricity off? (laughs) I swam towards the wire cable and then I grab, and then I managed to reach Kati. I had to get underneath her, and swim up strong to lift her up. (Macfarlane) Yes. (Buyisile Makhosonke) Kati pulled her in. That’s how we managed to save her. (Macfarlane) Thousands were left homeless after the floods, now housed in prefab homes like these. In the immediate aftermath of the flooding, Mak, Bond and their colleagues searched tirelessly for survivors… and retrieved the bodies of those who drowned. (Buyisile Makhosonke) I’m not a person, who if someone is in trouble, likes to sit back and watch. No. I want to be there. (Macfarlane) Why do you keep doing it? Why do you keep doing what you do? (Buyisile Makhosonke) What I’m doing, I love it.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): They call him Bond... K9 Bond - we meet the talented SAPS Search and Rescue dog named Bond, and explore the extraordinary relationship between hound and handler.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Bond is attached to the SAPS K9 search and rescue unit in the Eastern Cape, and by all accounts, this Belgian Malinois is one of the best in the business.In their relatively short career together, Bond and his handler Seargent Buyisile Makhosone – affectionately known as Mak – have made quite a name for themselves. Bond has even made an appearance in the Western Cape Provincial Parliament, where he was recognised for the significant role he played in the search for survivors during the devastating George Building collapse. But it is beautiful 'bond' between MAk and Bond that make this story worth telling - they're both young, dynamic and ready to take on whatever the job throws at them.
metadata.Summary: We had to go the full written approval route with the SAPS, and we've been approved for full access to Mak and Bond for two days. We've also got access to the whole Eastern Cape K9 unit, we can see training and demonstrations and do ride alongs etc if they are called out during our filming. We'll also get to speak to the head of the Easter Cape K9 unit. But the focus on the story will be getting to know both Mak and Bond - Sgt Makhosone is well spoken and passionate and I'm keen to find out what makes him tick.
metadata.Further information: MAk and Bond are stationed in Lusikisiki - a small town hours from the nearest airport in the Eastern Cape. The SAPS have agreed to bring them up to Mthatha for the filming - and Mthatha has an airport.
